newsitem.title: UK: UK house prices up at fastest rate since '88 - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK house prices up at fastest rate since '88 - survey.

text.p: British house prices are climbing at their fastest rate since 1988, seemingly immune to the uncertainties of a looming general election or fears of interest rate rises, a survey out on Tuesday said.

The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors said over 10 percent of chartered surveyors who contribute to the survey said house prices have risen by more than 5 percent over the three months to the end of March.
Aside from 1988, when the housing market was spiralling out of control, this is the first time that has happened since the survey began 20 years ago.

"The housing market seems to be immune to the election," said the surveyors housing market spokesman Ian Perry. "Even the widely predicted interest rate rise in early May and possible phasing out of MIRAS (mortgage interest relief) is unlikely to have any appreciable effect."

Labour's Gordon Brown, widely tipped to become Chancellor of the Exchequer after May 1 elections with the Labour Party still streets ahead in the polls, is expected to quickly raise interest rates to establish his anti-inflationary credentials.
Despite hefty price rises in some areas, the RICs said the housing recovery remained patchy with the market being led by buoyant conditions in London, the South East and the Midlands.
